newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico labor chief to head union into the 100s.
newsitem.headline: Mexico labor chief to head union into the 100s.

text.p: The leader of Mexico's main labour union, 96-year-old Fidel Velazquez, on Tuesday extended his rule for six more years, in a bid to remain one of Mexico's most powerful men even after he turns 100.

Amid internal divisions in his six million strong Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), delegates at a general assembly agreed to back Velazquez for a new term between 1998-2004, state news agency Notimex reported.
On Monday, union officials had said the decision would not be taken until next year, but it was apparently brought forward to avoid any potentially divisive power struggle.
Velazquez, who has reigned supreme over the labour movement for 50 years, was unchallenged by rival candidates, even though it would be his ninth successive six-year term.

He is a key pillar of the Institutional Revolutionary Party that has ruled Mexico for almost 68 straight years, pressuring members to vote for it even though under its watch living standards have fallen for nearly 20 unbroken years.

In proposing his re-election, one of the CTM's top officials, Leonardo Rodriguez Alcaine, acknowledged that Velazquez was fighting against time. During the assembly, he was visibly weak, his head hung even during a standing ovation, and he was unable to read his own keynote address.
The news agency said CTM leaders decided not to press on with a campaign to make Velazquez leader for life, because that conflicted with its own internal statutes.
But in a sign of his lingering power, he was given full authoritity to pick his own executive committee, it added.
